title: Safe Function Declaration & Hoisting Sandbox
concept: ES6 Annex B Block Scoping for Function Declarations
problemStatement: In ES6+, function declarations inside `if` blocks are block-scoped. Implement `evaluateBlockFunctions(condition, trueFnName, falseFnName)` that executes a simulated block-scoped environment and returns which function is accessible outside the block vs inside.
interviewTrap: In legacy ES5 / non-strict mode, function declarations in blocks were hoisted out into function scope, overwriting each other. In strict mode, they are strictly block scoped.

testCases.name: Functions are scoped and execute deterministically
testCases.testFn: const r1 = evaluateBlockFunctions(true); const r2 = evaluateBlockFunctions(false); return typeof r1.insideResult === 'string' && typeof r2.insideResult === 'string';

details.name: Functions are scoped and execute deterministically

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: A Hoisting & TDZ Sandbox safely evaluates dynamic code strings containing arbitrary var/let/const and function declarations, capturing TDZ violations and hoisting behaviors without crashing the parent execution context.
stepByStepWalkthrough: Construct an isolated execution scope using `new Function()` with trapped globals.
Instrument the code or catch runtime `ReferenceError`s resulting from premature access to uninitialized bindings.
Distinguish between standard undeclared variables (`ReferenceError: x is not defined`) and TDZ access errors (`ReferenceError: Cannot access 'x' before initialization`).
Return structured diagnostics detailing hoisted identifiers, TDZ traps encountered, and final return values.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: Function declarations in blocks (Annex B.3.3) have complex legacy hoisting semantics. Top-level function declarations are fully hoisted with their implementation during the Creation phase. `new Function` creates a fresh global-like script context that prevents local scope pollution.

complexity.time: O(E) execution time of evaluated code snippet.

edgeCasesHandled: Allowing hoisted function calls before declaration line.
Handling syntax errors vs runtime TDZ reference errors distinctly.

specifications: ECMA-262 Annex B.3.3 Block-Level Function Declarations Web Legacy Compatibility
ECMA-262 §19.2.1.1 Function ( p1, p2, … , pn, body ) (Dynamic function evaluation)
verifiedRules: Function declarations are hoisted with function body definition.
TDZ exceptions are distinct runtime ReferenceErrors originating from uninitialized environment slots.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How do class declarations behave regarding hoisting and the Temporal Dead Zone?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: Class declarations in JavaScript behave exactly like `let` declarations: they ARE hoisted to the top of their block, but remain in the TDZ until the class declaration statement evaluates. Attempting to instantiate a class (`new MyClass()`) before its declaration line throws `ReferenceError: Cannot access 'MyClass' before initialization`, even though class methods are defined.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Many candidates falsely assume classes hoist like function declarations.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: What are the Annex B.3.3 web legacy semantics for block-level function declarations?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In ES5 and sloppy (non-strict) mode, function declarations inside blocks (`if (cond) { function foo() {} }`) had browser-dependent undefined behavior. ES6 standardized Annex B.3.3: the function declaration creates a block-scoped binding hoisted to the block, BUT ALSO hoists a `var` binding to the enclosing function/global scope which receives the function value only when the block executes. In strict mode, function declarations are strictly block-scoped without outer pollution.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests knowledge of the darkest compatibility corners of the ECMAScript specification.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: Why does class Sub extends Super {} place Super in the TDZ?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: In a class `extends` clause, the superclass expression evaluates in the outer scope during class definition. If `Super` is declared with `let`/`class` below `Sub`, the extends expression evaluates `Super` while it is in the TDZ, resulting in a ReferenceError before the class body is even interpreted.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Tests understanding of class inheritance evaluation order.

howToExplain.opening: Class declarations and complex block-scoped constructs obey strict TDZ semantics, differentiating them from legacy function declarations.
keyPoints: Classes are never hoisted like function declarations; they behave like let bindings in the TDZ.
Function declarations in strict mode are block-scoped; in sloppy mode they follow Annex B legacy dual-hoisting.
Class extends clauses evaluate the superclass expression in the TDZ of the super identifier.
Sandboxed evaluation engines isolate these errors to prevent parent process crashes.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Mastering TDZ boundaries across classes, modules, and legacy block semantics is vital when debugging bundler output and circular dependency crashes.
analogies: A blueprint vs a building: a function declaration is a prefabricated building dropped in instantly; a class is a blueprint that must be formally registered before you can enter.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming class Foo {} hoists like function Foo() {}.
commonMistakes.why: Classes were deliberately specified in ES6 to follow let/const TDZ semantics to prevent calling constructors before prototype definitions are finalized.
commonMistakes.correct: State clearly that class declarations are hoisted into the TDZ and throw ReferenceError if accessed early.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does new.target behave in static class initialization blocks (ES2022)?
followUpDeepDive.answer: In ES2022 static initialization blocks (`static { ... }`), `new.target` is `undefined` because the block evaluates during class definition, not during instantiation. Variables declared with `let`/`const` inside static blocks are block-scoped to that initialization block, with their own TDZ.
followUpDeepDive.specReference: ECMA-262 §15.7 Class Definitions Static Initializer Blocks
